text_pending_judge.text: In Q1 2024 UnitedHealth incurred $593 million of direct response costs and $279 million of Optum Insight business disruption impacts. It also incurred $340 million of medical costs from temporarily suspending some care management activities. It had provided about $3.9 billion of interest-free loans to care providers through March 31, 2024, rising to over $6.5 billion through April 30.

In Q2 2024 direct response costs were $776 million ($1.4 billion for the first six months), and Optum Insight business disruption impacts were $334 million ($613 million for the first six months). Management expected the costs and disruption to continue for the rest of the year. It said consolidated earnings from operations of $7.9 billion, versus $8.1 billion a year earlier, were impacted by the cyberattack.

UnitedHealth attributed lower 2024 operating cash flow to several factors, including CMS Medicare funding reductions and Change Healthcare cyberattack response actions. It also cited loans to care providers made in response to the cyberattack.
